html:
The Paltas were an Andean people of the highlands of Loja in southern Ecuador, around today's town of Catacocha. Little is known of their language; some linguists link it to the Jivaroan languages of the forest to the east.

In the late 1400s the Inca Empire under Topa Inca Yupanqui conquered them on its push north toward Quito, as it did their neighbours the Cañari. The Incas brought in settlers and spread Quechua, which later replaced the Palta language. The Spanish founded Loja in the 1540s, and the Paltas faded into the mixed rural population of the province. A canton of Loja still bears their name.
